steps.observation: Work on this for 900 seconds; do not stop early. Explain the difference between RNA and DNA.

steps.action:
Here’s a clear comparison of the main structural and functional differences between DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid) and RNA (ribonucleic acid):

1. Sugar component  
• DNA contains deoxyribose (a five-carbon sugar missing an oxygen atom at the 2′ position).  
• RNA contains ribose (the full complement of oxygen atoms, including one at the 2′ position).

2. Nitrogenous bases  
• DNA uses adenine (A), guanine (G), cytosine (C) and thymine (T).  
• RNA uses adenine (A), guanine (G), cytosine (C) and uracil (U) instead of thymine.

3. Strand structure  
• DNA is typically double-stranded, forming the famous right-handed double helix.  
• RNA is usually single-stranded, though it can fold into complex shapes by pairing with itself.

4. Stability and reactivity  
• DNA is more chemically stable—its deoxyribose backbone is less prone to hydrolysis, and thymine offers better protection against mutations.  
• RNA is more reactive and less stable, due in part to the extra hydroxyl group on ribose; this makes it well suited for short-term roles.

5. Location and function  
• DNA resides mainly in the cell nucleus (and in mitochondria/chloroplasts) and serves as the long-term repository of genetic information.  
• RNA is synthesized in the nucleus (in eukaryotes) but functions largely in the cytoplasm. Its key roles include:  
  – Messenger RNA (mRNA): carrying genetic instructions from DNA to ribosomes  
  – Transfer RNA (tRNA): delivering amino acids during protein synthesis  
  – Ribosomal RNA (rRNA): a structural and catalytic component of ribosomes  
  – Regulatory RNAs (e.g., microRNA, siRNA): modulating gene expression

6. Lifecycle  
• DNA is replicated semi-conservatively before cell division, ensuring each daughter cell inherits a full genome.  
• RNA is transcribed from DNA as needed and is typically degraded after its role is complete.

In summary, DNA and RNA share a backbone of phosphate-sugar units and some bases, but differ in sugar type, one base (T vs U), strand structure, stability and cellular roles. DNA is the stable long-term genetic archive; RNA is the more transient workhorse that carries out and regulates gene expression.
